Who wrote it

How the writing of each article is spread across editors

Every word of today's text is credited to the editor who first added it. From that: how few people wrote most of an article, how much was written by editors Wikipedia itself later sanctioned, and how many editors write across many articles. Counts only; no editor is named on this page.

How concentrated the writing is

Each dot is one article: the share of today's text written by its main writer. A dot at 50% means one editor wrote half of the words readers see today.

one article (point at it for its name and figure; click to open it) the middle article of the area: half of its articles are to the left, half to the right. Its figure is printed at the end of the row

How many editors wrote half of the text

Number of articles, by the fewest editors who together wrote half of today's text

What “wrote” means

A word is credited to the editor who first typed it, followed through the whole history by WikiWho. Moving or restoring text does not make someone its author. Footnotes, tables and captions are left out.

Text by editors Wikipedia later sanctioned

Wikipedia's administrators ban some editors from a topic or from the site, or find them running extra accounts. Each dot is one article: the share of its text written by such editors. A sanction is about how someone behaved on Wikipedia, not proof that what they wrote is wrong.

Share of today's text by sanctioned editors, by topic area

Articles above 50% are drawn at the right edge.
